findings.claim: The claimed review branch and its anchor implementation could not be retrieved, so the artifact's cryptographic, operational, and line-level claims are presently unauditable rather than verified.
evidence: Repository search located the project security overview at https://github.com/G-0-B/FLOSS/security, but did not return the claimed branch, commits `0a34637` or `fbaae97`, or any claimed anchor files.

Direct retrieval attempts for `https://github.com/G-0-B/FLOSS/tree/reconcile/pr38-salvage-20260817`, `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/G-0-B/FLOSS/reconcile/pr38-salvage-20260817/packages/activity_log/anchor.py`, and `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/G-0-B/FLOSS/reconcile/pr38-salvage-20260817/scripts/provenance_anchor.py` returned: `Failed to fetch url content`.
This is a `could not retrieve` finding, not a claim that the branch or files do not exist.
findings.falsifier: A publicly retrievable immutable commit URL, tarball, or raw-file URLs resolving to the stated branch and files, permitting inspection of the exact source and tests.

findings.claim: The assertion that the mechanism has 25 passing tests and produces the listed verification outcomes is unsupported by independently retrievable test evidence.
evidence: The claimed test path was not available in the retrieved repository search results; no result exposed `packages/activity_log/tests/test_anchor.py`, its test output, or CI run associated with commits `0a34637` or `fbaae97`.
The only located repository result identifies the project but supplies no test execution, workflow result, commit state, or anchor implementation evidence: https://github.com/G-0-B/FLOSS/security
This is a `could not retrieve` finding, not a claim that the test file, tests, or passing run do not exist.
findings.falsifier: A reproducible checkout pinned to `0a34637` or `fbaae97`, plus complete command output for the anchor test suite and any required fixture-generation steps.

findings.claim: No conclusion about whether the custom Merkle construction is safe, whether its signature scope is complete, or whether it can yield false `VERIFIED` outcomes can be grounded because the implementation and specification text were unavailable.
evidence: No retrieved source exposed the required code for leaf serialization, integer parsing, BLAKE3 domain-prefix application, odd-node handling, empty-tree construction, scan semantics, signature canonicalization, atomic file handling, or verification outcome selection.
No retrieved source exposed the stated specification's section 7 or its line numbers; therefore the stated-limits completeness claim cannot be compared against actual normative text.
The accessible repository search result provides only a generic GitHub repository/security page, not these source files: https://github.com/G-0-B/FLOSS/security
findings.falsifier: Retrievable source at the claimed revision, including the implementation, specification, existing packet validator, fixtures, dependency lockfiles, and test output.

predicted_majority: Other reviewers with access to the claimed revision will likely focus on the lack of independently verified third-party retention and on the custom-build-versus-adopt decision; this review cannot validate or refute those substantive claims because the cited artifact was not retrievable.
where_you_expect_to_be_alone: The strongest present finding is evidentiary: treating a non-retrievable tier-2 emergency artifact as reviewed would violate the requested retrieval-grounded audit standard, regardless of whether its prose description is technically plausible.
